blocks.content: Building on the concept introduced in the Environment Variables module, Docker secrets is Docker Swarm's native mechanism for handling sensitive values properly, encrypted at rest, and never exposed as a plain environment variable.
In a Swarm cluster, docker secret create stores a sensitive value (a password, an API key) encrypted within the swarm's internal store, entirely separate from any service's configuration or image.

blocks.alt: Stored encrypted, separate from any service definition

blocks.content: 2. Delivered as a File, Never an Environment Variable
blocks.text: 2. Delivered as a File, Never an Environment Variable

blocks.content: This is the core design decision that fixes the problem covered in the Environment Variables module: a Docker secret is mounted into the container as a file under /run/secrets/, readable only by the process that needs it, never visible via docker inspect or a process environment dump.

blocks.alt: A file the process reads, not a variable anything can inspect

blocks.content:
services:
  app:
    secrets: [db_password]
secrets:
  db_password:
    external: true

# Inside the container:
cat /run/secrets/db_password

code.content:

  app:
    secrets: [db_password]

blocks.content: 3. Encrypted Both at Rest and in Transit
blocks.text: 3. Encrypted Both at Rest and in Transit

blocks.content: Beyond just being file-based, Swarm secrets are encrypted while stored, and encrypted again as they are distributed to the specific nodes that actually need them, a meaningfully stronger guarantee than a value sitting in plain text in an environment variable or a config file.

blocks.alt: Real encryption, both stored and while being distributed

blocks.content: 4. The Concrete Difference From an Env Var
blocks.text: 4. The Concrete Difference From an Env Var

blocks.content: Put side by side, the practical gap is stark: an environment variable holding a secret is visible to anything that can inspect the container, a Docker secret simply is not exposed that way at all.

blocks.alt: Inspectable versus genuinely hidden from that entire class of exposure

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Docker secrets store sensitive values encrypted and deliver them as files under /run/secrets, never as an inspectable environment variable.
This is a Swarm-native feature, teams not using Swarm typically reach for an external secrets manager instead, but the underlying principle, files over env vars, applies everywhere.
